reason: Tampa Bay has been mashing right-handed pitching, at a 161 wRC+ over its last 6 and 144 over its last 12 — both elite and pointing the same way. Bassitt is a contact-oriented arm (11.9 K% over his last 3, 10.4 Barrel%) who hasn't started in 72 days and threw only 56 pitches his last time out, so he isn't stretched and figures for a short leash, and TBR has scored 5 and 3 earned in his last two meetings against them. Once he exits, Baltimore's bullpen sits at a 5.90 ERA over its last 12. Getting plus money on a top-form lineup against a rusty pitcher and a leaking bullpen is the value.

Pittsburgh cannot hit left-handed pitching, sitting at a 59 wRC+ over its last 6 and 61 over its last 12 vs LHP — an established, not streaky, weakness, with a 30.9 K% over that span. Bennett carries a 2.62 xERA over his last 3 that his 5.19 ERA badly understates, meaning the market is pricing a pitcher who has actually been much better. Behind him Boston's bullpen owns a 2.34 xERA over its last 12. A punchless lineup against a quietly excellent starter and an elite bullpen should struggle to reach four runs.

The Cubs are crushing left-handed pitching at a 160 wRC+ over their last 6 and 162 over their last 12 — elite and fully established. Liberatore is a modest lefty (3.13 xERA but only 4.9 IP/gs over his last 3) whom Chicago squared up for 8 hits and 3 runs in 3.2 innings his last time facing them. His short outings hand the game to a St. Louis bullpen carrying a 4.70 xERA over its last 12. Even money on the league's hottest lineup against a hittable lefty and a soft bullpen is the price to take.

San Francisco has been historically helpless against left-handed pitching, posting a -28 wRC+ over its last 6 and just 16 over its last 12 vs LHP with a 36.2 K% — both windows catastrophic. Freeland brings a 3.15 xERA over his last 3 into a pitcher-friendly park. Getting plus money on the under for a lineup that essentially cannot score against lefties, facing a solid one, is a clear mispricing.

Cincinnati is striking out at a 32.9% clip against right-handed pitching over its last 6 while scuffling to a 77 wRC+, exactly the whiff-prone profile a strikeout over feeds on. Alcantara has a 23.7 K% over his last 3 with 5, 5, and 8 punchouts, and he goes deep — 6.7 IP/gs — with the outs line set at 18.5, giving him the length to clear the number. A high-K opponent plus a durable arm makes 5.5 too low at even money.
